definition: A configuration value set before training begins (such as learning rate or batch size) that is not learned from the data itself.
details: Hyperparameter tuning, via grid search, random search, or Bayesian optimization, is a key part of building effective models.
story: Think of a hiker descending a foggy hill in the dark, taking small steps and feeling for the steepest way down. The machine starts out clumsy, makes mistakes, and is nudged a little less wrong every time. It is the same loop you use to learn anything: try, miss, correct, try again. Skill, for a model, is just error pushed down until it is small enough to ignore. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Hyperparameter.
